finding.claim: The authenticated identity is read directly from a client-supplied HTTP header (X-Session-User-Verified) with no signature, session lookup or token check in this code. Every ACL decision depends on this value, so any client that can reach the app can impersonate any user, including a resource owner, and delete or rename their files. The header's name suggests an upstream proxy sets it. This is only safe if that proxy strips and overwrites the header on every inbound request. Nothing in the repo enforces that.
finding.source: Request header X-Session-User-Verified, set by any unauthenticated remote client
finding.sink: ensure_allowed/is_allowed in delete_file (del STORE[fid]) and rename_file (f['name'] = ...), which look up resource['grants'][g.user]

trace.note: g.user = request.headers.get('X-Session-User-Verified'), taken verbatim from the request
is_allowed checks action in grants.get(user, []), so a spoofed username inherits that user's grants
del STORE[fid] runs once the spoofed identity passes the check
rename_file uses the same g.user for its 'write' check
The file name is overwritten after the spoofed identity passes

finding.guards_checked: The ACL is enforced per resource on both routes, so authorization is present. Authentication is the gap: no signature or session validation, no proxy-stripping logic and no other before_request hook exists in the repo. A missing header gives g.user=None, which has no grants, so anonymous requests are denied. The bypass needs a header naming a user who holds grants.

verdict.guard_found: ACL checks only: ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10, aborts 403) and is_allowed (acl.py:5, result tested at views.py:25). Both are correctly used, but they trust g.user. There is no signature or session validation and no proxy-stripping logic in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (views.py:11 sets g.user from the client header, and the ACL calls at views.py:17 and :25 gate the effects at :18 and :27). Whether an outside client can spoof the header depends on whether an upstream proxy strips and overwrites X-Session-User-Verified. That deployment detail is not in the repo, which contains only acl.py and views.py.
